explanation: The callable receives the selected node and a new node. First point the new node to the selected node’s old successor, then point the selected node to the new node.
timeComplexity: O(p): advance to one-based position p, then perform two constant-time link changes.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary pointers plus exactly one newly allocated node.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/insert_in_list.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Saving the successor in new_node.next before changing node.next keeps the suffix reachable. The two rewired links insert exactly the supplied node without replacing any original node or changing their relative order.
walkthrough: Case [7,4,9], position 2, new value 6 selects node 4 using one-based indexing. The wrapper allocates node 6. The callable sets 6.next=9, then 4.next=6 and returns no value; the wrapper observes [7,4,6,9].
edgeCases: Position 1 means insert after the head, not before it.
Inserting after the last node appends a new tail.
Existing nodes and their values are retained.
